macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks closed higher but ended the week lower as investors watched bond yields and Middle East tensions
items.summary: The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all finished Friday in the green, but each posted weekly declines as volatility in Treasury yields and geopolitical uncertainty weighed on sentiment. Strong August U.S. services-sector data also helped support the late-week rebound.

items.title: Treasury buyback announcement helped briefly steady markets amid rising long-term yields
items.summary: U.S. equities fell over the week as the 30-year Treasury yield moved above 5.3% earlier in the week, driven by fiscal and inflation concerns. The Treasury said it would double or more its buybacks of longer-dated securities, a move that briefly eased pressure on markets.

items.title: Jackson Hole, Nvidia earnings and key inflation data are the main market focuses for the week ahead
items.summary: Markets are watching the Jackson Hole symposium, Nvidia's earnings report, and several major U.S. data releases including PCE inflation, GDP revisions, durable goods orders, and consumer confidence. These events are expected to shape expectations for growth, rates and AI-related equities.

items.title: U.S. and Canada failed to reach a trade deal, with Washington set to impose 50% tariffs on some Canadian imports
items.summary: The White House said it would impose 50-percent tariffs on certain imports from Canada after talks broke down. Canada said it would retaliate and suspend trade negotiations, adding a new trade-policy risk for markets.

items.title: Nvidia, CrowdStrike, Salesforce and Marvell are among the week’s major earnings watches
items.summary: Investors are awaiting marquee earnings from Nvidia on Wednesday, followed by CrowdStrike, Salesforce and Marvell, as the market looks for confirmation of AI infrastructure and semiconductor demand trends.

items.title: Global economic activity strengthened in August, with U.S. business activity leading
items.summary: Flash PMI data showed the U.S. as the clear growth leader, with services strength driving a faster pace of business activity and raising estimates for third-quarter growth. The report also noted firmer employment and robust demand.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin slips under $77,000 after recent rally
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $76,536 on Sunday, down 0.8% over 24 hours after briefly reaching $77,468, while Ether, XRP, BNB and Cardano were mostly lower and Solana edged up. The move came as investors weighed improved miner profitability and commentary from Grayscale that the bear market may be maturing.

items.title: Crypto market sees sharp weekend selloff, with heavy liquidations
items.summary: A weekend crypto drop pushed Bitcoin lower, Ether down 5.29%, XRP down 12.21% and Cardano down 14.05%, alongside nearly 179,200 liquidations totaling about $882 million in 24 hours. Reports linked the earlier rally to Treasury buyback expansion and a Trump meeting with crypto leaders, but the latest move reversed much of that optimism.

items.title: XRP flash crash triggers major crypto liquidations
items.summary: XRP reportedly fell as much as 37% within minutes, with about $500 million in long positions liquidated. The broader crypto market saw roughly $1.35 billion in liquidations over the last 24 hours, according to Coinglass data cited in the report.

items.title: Wall Street flows into altcoins as XRP, SOL and HYPE rally
items.summary: One report said nearly $90 million flowed into altcoin products as XRP, Solana and HYPE moved higher. XRP was described as rising roughly 50% from below $1 earlier in the week to as high as $1.60.

items.title: TRUMP token drops after team moves millions to exchanges
items.summary: The TRUMP cryptocurrency fell 33% after the project team moved $6.2 million to exchanges following a recent surge. The report framed the move as part of a broader volatile run in which Bitcoin gained $15,000 in less than 48 hours.

items.title: South Korea blocks access to Polymarket over illegal gambling concerns
items.summary: Reports said South Korea ordered a block on Polymarket after determining the crypto prediction market constituted an illegal gambling environment for users. This is one of the clearest regulatory actions in the latest 24-hour window.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI cuts developer pricing for GPT-5.6 Sol by more than 20%
items.summary: OpenAI reduced API pricing for its frontier GPT-5.6 Sol model and said the cuts also apply to eligible ChatGPT Work and Codex plans. The move points to intensifying price competition in enterprise AI infrastructure and developer tooling.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic pivot on enterprise privacy
items.summary: Both companies are reportedly making privacy-focused changes that challenge or reverse earlier positions, signaling that enterprise data handling has become a key battleground in AI. The shift suggests privacy is now a central competitive differentiator for foundation-model providers.

items.title: OpenAI makes ChatGPT less 'human' for teens
items.summary: OpenAI rolled out a safety update that changes how ChatGPT interacts with teenage users. The announcement underscores continued industry pressure to add age-specific safeguards and reduce risky emotional dependence on AI assistants.

items.title: A mysterious model called Ox Alpha appears on OpenRouter
items.summary: Ox Alpha, an unidentified AI model, debuted on OpenRouter, drawing attention because of its unclear origin and capabilities. The appearance of a strong anonymous model highlights how quickly new entrants can surface through model hubs and benchmarking communities.

items.title: Google expands AI education tools and offers free AI Plus access to eligible students
items.summary: Google announced new AI-powered learning tools for the 2026 academic year and a 12-month free Google AI Plus plan for eligible college students outside the US. The package indicates a push to lock in student adoption as AI becomes embedded in education workflows.

items.title: Murf AI launches Falcon 2 text-to-speech model
items.summary: Murf AI unveiled Falcon 2, a text-to-speech model designed for more human-like voices at lower cost and faster speed. The company says it targets enterprise use cases such as call centers, banks, and airlines, reflecting continued momentum in voice AI.

items.title: Wispr Flow raises $280 million and previews speech model Canto
items.summary: San Francisco-based Wispr Flow raised $280 million at a $2 billion valuation and introduced a preview of its proprietary speech model, Canto. The funding round shows investor appetite remains strong for speech AI and productivity-focused voice interfaces.

items.title: Sebi prepares responsible AI and machine learning guidelines for securities markets
items.summary: India's markets regulator said it will soon issue AI and ML guidelines with safeguards including a kill switch, human oversight, and data controls. The framework is meant to support AI adoption in surveillance, risk assessment, fraud detection, and investor services while preserving accountability.

items.title: Alibaba raises $10 billion amid renewed AI competition
items.summary: Alibaba is seeking about HK$80 billion in a share sale as part of its push to compete for global AI leadership. The financing effort reflects how AI expansion is influencing capital markets and spending plans across major tech firms.

items.title: China’s embodied AI progress highlighted by humanoid robot race
items.summary: A Chinese humanoid robot ran a 100-meter dash faster than Usain Bolt’s world-record time, although it later crashed into a wall. The event highlights rapid progress in embodied AI and robotics, alongside clear limits in control and stability.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Take-Two subpoenas Discord and Microsoft in GTA VI leak hunt
items.summary: Take-Two is pursuing subpoenas to identify the source of a Grand Theft Auto VI leak, with Discord and Microsoft among the companies named in the effort. The move highlights how major publishers are escalating legal action around high-profile game leaks.

items.title: South of Midnight developer Compulsion Games becomes independent again
items.summary: Compulsion Games, the studio behind South of Midnight, has reportedly completed a management buyout and is independent from Microsoft again. The change is a notable shift in Xbox’s studio structure and ownership landscape.

items.title: Nioh 3 announced for 2026 with PS5 demo available now
items.summary: Nioh 3 is reportedly coming in 2026, and players can try a demo on PlayStation 5 immediately. The announcement gives the action RPG series a concrete next step and an early hands-on opportunity for fans.

items.title: Xbox rumored to be working on a new Ori game
items.summary: A prominent leaker claims Xbox is developing a new Ori game, six years after Ori and the Will of the Wisps. If accurate, it would mark the return of one of Xbox’s most acclaimed platforming series.

items.title: Game releases and announcements surface across regional gaming coverage
items.summary: Recent coverage includes new game reveals such as Heatwarped, Planet Architect, and Sanguine Shock, along with release-date news for titles like SiN Reloaded and console versions of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+. Several of these items point to a busy slate of indie and mid-tier releases moving through storefront and event announcements.

items.title: GTA 6 leak drama intensifies with fresh threat messaging online
items.summary: A new report says the GTA 6 leak figure known as CyberLeek posted a fresh threat aimed at Rockstar Games. The episode keeps Grand Theft Auto VI at the center of both security and community controversy ahead of release.
